MutSalpha._status: DISABLED 2026-09-07, superseded by the MSH2 and MSH6 entries. The structures, labels and AlphaMissense data are unchanged and still correct; this entry is retained for provenance and for reproducing the merged descriptor.
MutSalpha._why_disabled: load_protein_configs() is iterated WHOLESALE -- run.py passes every config to build_d1_table with no dataset filter, and build_configured_external_gt loops all of them. Left enabled alongside MSH2/MSH6 it put the same 147 variants into the D1 table twice (151 + 109 + 42 = 302 rows for 147 variants) under two identities, which inflates pooled counts and, worse, leaks: holding out MSH2 would leave the same MSH2 variants in training as MutSalpha rows. Unlike metric_analysis/protein_configs.json -- where the MutS_alpha entry MUST stay, because the structure-metrics pipeline still runs on it and MSH2/MSH6 read its distribution summary -- nothing here needs it.
MutSalpha._to_reproduce_merged: set enabled to true and disable MSH2 and MSH6, so the two layouts are never active at once.

MSH2._status: ENABLED. MSH2 is one subunit of the modelled MutSalpha heterodimer, split out as its own dataset (2026-09-07). Structures, chain and wild-type reference are shared with MSH6; the descriptor is restricted to MSH2's own residue rows.
MSH2._split_rationale: The merged MutSalpha dataset averaged every descriptor over all 2,294 residues of MSH2+MSH6 regardless of which subunit carried the mutation, so 59% of an MSH2 variant's D1 and 41% of an MSH6 variant's came from the unmutated partner. Merged AUC 0.701 was an average of two unlike datasets (MSH2 0.822, MSH6 0.625 under the merged descriptor). See experiments/mutsalpha_subunit_split/.
MSH2._shared_wild_type: MutS_alpha_WT_plddt_values.csv is the single wild-type ensemble for both datasets: one prediction of the complex represents both native subunits. Each dataset reads its own rows out of it.
MSH2.data_revision: 2026-10-15 v6_ca: WT is C-alpha (was backbone N) and regenerated with the variants' templates

MSH6._status: ENABLED. MSH6 is one subunit of the modelled MutSalpha heterodimer, split out as its own dataset (2026-09-07); the descriptor is restricted to MSH6's own residue rows. MSH6._split_rationale: The merged MutSalpha dataset averaged every descriptor over all 2,294 residues of MSH2+MSH6 regardless of which subunit carried the mutation, so 59% of an MSH2 variant's D1 and 41% of an MSH6 variant's came from the unmutated partner. Merged AUC 0.701 was an average of two unlike datasets (MSH2 0.822, MSH6 0.625 under the merged descriptor). See experiments/mutsalpha_subunit_split/.
MSH6._shared_wild_type: MutS_alpha_MSH6_GT_WT_plddt_values.csv is MSH6's wild type: the same MSH2-MSH6 complex folded on the 21/21-nt G:T duplex its variants use. Until 2026-10-12 MSH6 shared MSH2's MutS_alpha_WT, whose 21/20-nt duplex did not match the old MSH6 batch's 136/137-nt one.
